name: Uchiravaneswarar Temple, Tiruvilanagar
deity: Shiva as Uchiravaneswarar (Vizharkaattu Nathar, Thurai Kattum Vallalar), with the goddess Veyuru Tholi Ammai
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tiruvilanagar, near Mayiladuthurai, honours Shiva as Uchiravaneswarar — also Vizharkaattu Nathar, lord of the reed forest — with the goddess Veyuru Tholi Ammai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, it stands among the Shiva shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The temple's name recalls the vizhal reeds that once grew thick here, the lord revered as the one who 'shows the ford' to his devotees.

sections.history: Tiruvilanagar, near Mayiladuthurai, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Kaveri's southern bank, its Shiva hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. Older directories place it in Nagapattinam district; after the district reorganisation it falls within Mayiladuthurai district. The stone temple belongs to the Chola period and after, raised over the ancient sacred site that the saint's hymns had already made famous.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta shrine, the temple enshrines Uchiravaneswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Veyuru Tholi Ammai in her own shrine, a Nandi, and the customary parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the vizhal, the reed or spear-grass; the Sanskrit uchira gives the lord the name Uchiravaneswarar, and in Tamil he is Vizharkaattu Nathar, lord of the reed forest. The temple is grouped among the Mayiladuthurai Pancha Dakshinamurti sthalams.
sections.legends: The sthala purana recalls a time when vizhal reeds grew thick over this ground, within which the lingam was found and worshipped — hence the lord's names Uchiravaneswarar and Vizharkaattu Nathar. He is also praised as Thurai Kattum Vallalar, the generous one who 'shows the ford,' guiding his devotees across the waters of samsara. As with the smaller delta shrines, the fuller sthala legends are preserved chiefly in the local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October), and the Mondays of Karthikai, with the regular Pradosha worship. These are kept at the modest scale of a village shrine, visited by pilgrims following the Paadal Petra trail of the southern Kaveri.
sections.experience: Tiruvilanagar offers the pilgrim a quiet Tevaram shrine amid the reed-country of the delta. Before Uchiravaneswarar and Veyuru Tholi Ammai, the visitor meets the 'lord who shows the ford' — a small temple whose ancient name and surviving worship carry the memory of the reed forest in which it first rose.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvilanagar (Arupathi post, PIN 609309) is about 7–11 km from Mayiladuthurai on the Mayiladuthurai–Tarangambadi road. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest rail head, with buses toward Tarangambadi passing nearby.
